en: Contrary to popular belief, Mount Apo, not Mount Mayon, is the highest mountain in the Philippines.
Although Mindanao is the second-largest, Luzon is actually the largest and most populous island in the Philippines.
Taal Volcano is not a simple peak, but a complex volcano featuring a main crater lake inside a larger caldera.
The Philippine eagle does not live exclusively in Mindanao, but also inhabits forests in Samar, Leyte, and Luzon.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is not located near Palawan's coast, but sits isolated in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
Many think Manila is the largest city, but Davao City actually holds the title for the largest land area in the Philippines.
While the Philippines experiences typhoons annually, they do not occur evenly year-round, with most forming between July and October.
Although Lake Lanao is the largest in Mindanao, Laguna de Bay is actually the largest lake in the entire Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were not built by Spanish colonizers, but were carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people.
The Chocolate Hills are not actual mountains, but rather cone-shaped karst limestone hills formed from ancient marine deposits.
The Pasig River is not the longest in the Philippines, as the Cagayan River holds that title at 505 kilometers.
Despite its legendary folklore, Mount Makiling is classified as an inactive volcano, meaning it has not erupted in recorded history.
